blogs.title: Beyond the Binary: Why 'Type 1.5' Isn't Enough and When to Suspect MODY in Young Adults
blogs.description: This post addresses the diagnostic dilemma of young patients who don't fit the classic Type 1 (autoimmune, DKA-prone) or Type 2 (obese, insulin-resistant) molds. Using the case of a lean young man with glycosuria but negative antibodies, we explore the clinical red flags for Maturity-Onset Diabetes of the Young (MODY), including the limitations of BMI and family history in diverse populations, and why the Exeter Probability Calculator may need calibration for non-European cohorts.

blogs.title: The Sulfonylurea Dogma vs. Modern Precision: Re-evaluating First-Line Therapy for HNF1A-MODY
blogs.description: While low-dose sulfonylureas have long been the gold standard for HNF1A-MODY, this post analyzes emerging evidence supporting GLP-1 receptor agonists as a viable, perhaps safer, alternative. We dissect the case's successful transition from insulin to dulaglutide, discussing mechanisms of action, hypoglycemia risks, beta-cell preservation, and how genetic confirmation allows clinicians to de-escalate from aggressive insulin regimens to targeted oral or injectable therapies.

blogs.title: The Renal Threshold Clue: Interpreting Glycosuria Without Hyperglycemic Crisis
blogs.description: A unique physiological feature of HNF1A mutations is a lowered renal threshold for glucose reabsorption due to downregulated SGLT2 expression. This post focuses on recognizing disproportionate glycosuria as a key bedside clue for HNF1A-MODY, even before severe hyperglycemia sets in. We also discuss the critical safety warning regarding SGLT2 inhibitors in these patients, explaining why a drug class common in Type 2 diabetes could precipitate euglycemic DKA or severe dehydration in this specific genetic subgroup.

blogs.title: Novel Variants and NGS: Navigating Uncertainty When the Database Comes Up Empty
blogs.description: Genetic testing often returns variants of uncertain significance or novel mutations not found in ClinVar. Using the identification of the novel p.N270S mutation in this case, this post guides clinicians on applying ACMG guidelines to interpret 'new' findings. We cover how to weigh segregation analysis within families, computational predictions (like AlphaMissense scores), and domain location to confidently diagnose monogenic diabetes even without a previously catalogued mutation.

blogs.title: Autonomic Neuropathy at Diagnosis? The Hidden Complications of Delayed Monogenic Diabetes Recognition
blogs.description: It is commonly assumed that monogenic diabetes has a benign course regarding microvascular complications compared to Type 1 or Type 2. However, this case presents a young patient with severely reduced sudomotor function at the time of diagnosis. This post challenges the assumption of 'benign' MODY, exploring how years of undiagnosed hyperglycemia due to misclassification can lead to early autonomic dysfunction, emphasizing that timely genetic diagnosis is not just about drug selection but preventing irreversible organ damage.
